key_insight: Curiosity-0826-4B extends zero-shot medical event prediction to pediatric populations and adult mortality, while reducing laboratory prediction error by 18–46% versus its predecessor.
clinical_relevance: A shared model could support prediction across ages and outcomes without separate task-specific training, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Generative foundation model trained on Epic Cosmos to simulate patient timelines.
Expanded clinical event representations, including documented death.
Scaled to 4.3B parameters and a 16K context window using scaling-law-guided pretraining.
evidence_signal: In evaluations covering ages 2–17, AUROCs were 0.742–0.785 for new asthma diagnosis, 0.829–0.852 for asthma exacerbation, and 0.820–0.847 for sickle cell crisis; adult mortality AUROCs were 0.821–0.942.
watch_item: Local calibration, subgroup performance, generalization, and prospective clinical utility require further validation before deployment.
paper_title: Curiosity-0826-4B: Generative Medical Event Sequence Modeling Across Pediatric and Adult Populations
